title: All Men Are Equal in Their Birth
description: All Men Are Equal in Their Birth in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Harriet Martineau wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 182, “Christian Equality”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: All men are e-qual in their birth, Heirs of the earth and skies; All men are e-qual, when that earth Fails from their dy-ing eyes.

lines: All men are equal in their birth,
Heirs of the earth and skies;
All men are equal, when that earth
Fails from their dying eyes.
God greets the throngs who pay their vows
In courts their hands have made;
And hears the worshipper who bows
Beneath the plantain shade.
'Tis man alone who difference sees,
And speaks of high and low;
And worships those, and tramples these,
While the same path they go.
O, let man hasten to restore
To all their rights of love!
In power and wealth exult no more,
In wisdom lowly move.
Ye great! renounce your earth-born pride;
Ye low! your shame and fear;
Live, as ye worship, side by side;
Your brotherhood revere.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Harriet Martineau died in 1876.
credits: Words by Harriet Martineau (1802–1876), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
